title: Bastionless Egress Fabric Terraform module for VPC security controls
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a composable Terraform module that provides a 'bastionless egress fabric' for private VPC deployments: automated security group templates, coordinated stateless NACL layer, private DNS stub routing for internal service discovery, and enforced egress policies (allow lists + optional egress-proxy hooks). The goal is a reusable, well-documented module teams can drop into Private/On‑prem deployments to satisfy regulatory network boundaries without requiring jump hosts or manual network config.
acceptance_criteria: Module can be instantiated with a single Terraform call to wire security-groups, NACLs, private DNS zone links, and egress policy objects for an existing VPC
Defaults enforce least-privilege egress: all outbound TCP/UDP denied except explicit allow rules and proxy port exceptions
Health-checking resources (internal egress-proxy endpoint, DNS resolution) are created and exposed via outputs for Console monitoring
Module has automated upgrade guidance: major/minor inputs to control behavior changes and a documented migration path
Integration tests validate NACL+SG behavior across typical flow patterns (control-plane to model nodes, model nodes to telemetry, admin CIDRs for management)
Module passes Terraform fmt, validate, and registry schema linting and is published to private module registry with versioned tags
tasks: Design TF module public API (inputs/outputs) and composability primitives
Implement security group templates and variable-driven rule sets
Implement coordinated stateless NACL generator with ordering guarantees
Add private DNS zone association helpers and stub resolver policy
Add egress policy resource with optional egress-proxy hooks and allow-list enforcement
Write integration tests using localstack/terraform-integration harness
Add health-check resources and outputs for Console: egress-proxy heartbeat, DNS lookup probe, NACL drift sensor
Document upgrade notes and migration playbook for existing Privnet customers
Create example environments (dev/stage/prod) and demo runbook
Code review, security review, and publish to private registry
decisions: Use composable submodules: sg, nacl, dns, egress-policy so teams can opt-in to pieces
Stateless NACL layer retained to provide network-level hard deny; SGs remain primary L7 intent surface
Default egress behavior is deny-all with allow-lists. Customers can opt to route through an egress-proxy by enabling module flag.
We will not bake in a specific egress proxy implementation; instead provide hook variables and small reference implementation using Envoy for customers who want a managed pattern
Module will emit monitoring-ready outputs (ARNs/URLs) and a small set of CloudWatch/Prometheus metrics for Console ingestion
testing_plan: Unit: terraform validate + fmt + tflint on each commit
Integration: spin up example VPC in ephemeral account, apply module, run connectivity matrix tests (from control-plane IPs to model subnets and to telemetry endpoints)
Chaos: simulate instance replacement and assert NACL rules remain deterministic and no transient egress leakage
Security: run policy-as-code checks (opa/rego) and internal pen-test on sample environment
Upgrade: test zero-downtime minor upgrades and documented manual steps for breaking changes
rollout_plan: Stage 1: internal infra team uses module in dev VPCs only
Stage 2: apply to stage environments with telemetry enabled and monitor for blocked egress alerts
Stage 3: opt-in pilot with one customer using Dedicated capacity; run canary for two weeks
Stage 4: wider rollout with migration playbook and support runbooks available
Rollback: module supports deterministic destroy/apply with preserved state; rollback steps documented in playbook
monitoring_and_health_checks: DNS probe: periodic lookup of internal service names via module-provisioned resolver and metric exported
Egress-proxy heartbeat: health endpoint that toggles a metric indicating outbound path health
NACL drift sensor: periodic terraform plan across core network resources to detect out-of-band changes
SG rule audit: snapshot outputs used by Console to show token-level risk exposure for instances behind SGs
